en.q: Lungs do not collapse between breaths and some air always remains in the lungs which can never be expelled because :
o: There is a negative pressure in the lungs
There is a negative intrapleural pressure pulling at the lung walls
There is a positive intrapleural pressure
Pressure in the lungs is higher than the atmospheric pressure
en.sol: The pleural fluid-filled space has a pressure below that in the lungs (negative intrapleural pressure). The chest wall pulls outward and the elastic lung pulls inward; this suction keeps the lungs from collapsing, so some air (residual volume) always stays. Answer: negative intrapleural pressure pulling at the lung walls. (Intrapleural pressure is not described in NCERT 14.2.)

en.q: Which of the following is not the function of conducting part of respiratory system ?
o: Temperature of inhaled air is brought to body temperature
Provides surface for diffusion of O<sub>2</sub> and CO<sub>2</sub>
It clears inhaled air from foreign particles
en.sol: NCERT 14.1.1: the conducting part (external nostrils to terminal bronchioles) transports air to the alveoli, clears it of foreign particles, humidifies it and brings it to body temperature. Diffusion of O2 and CO2 happens in the exchange (respiratory) part — the alveoli.

hi.q: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा श्वसन तंत्र के चालन भाग का कार्य नहीं है?

O<sub>2</sub> तथा CO<sub>2</sub> के विसरण के लिए सतह प्रदान करता है

en.q:
Match List I with List II :
A. Expiratory capacity — I. Expiratory reserve volume + Tidal volume + Inspiratory reserve volume
B. Functional residual capacity — II. Tidal volume + Expiratory reserve volume
C. Vital capacity — III. Tidal volume + Inspiratory reserve volume
D. Inspiratory capacity — IV. Expiratory reserve volume + Residual volume
en.sol:
• A. Expiratory capacity EC = TV + ERV — II.
  • B. Functional residual capacity FRC = ERV + RV — IV.

en.q:
Match List I with List II :
A. Molluscs — I. Pulmonary respiration only
B. Reptiles — II. Branchial respiration
C. Adult amphibians — III. Cellular respiration
D. Amoeba — IV. Pulmonary and Cutaneous respiration
en.sol:
• A. Molluscs (aquatic) breathe by gills — branchial respiration (II; NCERT 14.1).
  • B. Reptiles breathe by lungs only — pulmonary (I).
  • C. Adult amphibians (frogs) use lungs and moist skin — pulmonary and cutaneous (IV).
  • D. Amoeba exchanges gases directly by its cell surface (simple diffusion) — taken here as cellular respiration (III).

en.q:
In humans, respiration occurs in the following steps. Arrange these steps in the correct order :
A. Diffusion of O2 and CO2 between blood and tissues
B. Diffusion of O2 and CO2 across alveolar membrane
C. Pulmonary ventilation by which atmospheric air is drawn in and CO2 rich alveolar air is released out
D. Cellular respiration
E. Transport of gases by the blood
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
en.sol:
NCERT 14.1.1 lists the steps of respiration in order:

  1. C — pulmonary ventilation;
  2. B — diffusion across the alveolar membrane;
  3. E — transport of gases by blood;
  4. A — diffusion between blood and tissues;
  5. D — cellular respiration (use of O2 by cells).

C, B, E, A, D.
en.hint: Air in → lungs → blood → tissues → cells.

D. कोशिकीय श्वसन
E. रक्त द्वारा गैसों का परिवहन
नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए :
hi.sol:
NCERT 14.1.1 श्वसन के चरण क्रम से बताती है:

  1. C — फुप्फुसी संवातन;
  2. B — कूपिका झिल्ली के आर-पार विसरण;
  3. E — रक्त द्वारा गैसों का परिवहन;
  4. A — रक्त और ऊतकों के बीच विसरण;
  5. D — कोशिकीय श्वसन (कोशिकाओं द्वारा O2 का उपयोग)।

C, B, E, A, D।
